title: External reader never sees internal identifiers, metric values, or dependency names on the status page
asA: security-conscious external reader (and the security reviewer for the deployed application)
iWant: the public status page to expose only the declared component vocabulary and the incident notice fields
soThat: internal topology and performance detail is not committed as public contract and does not become reconnaissance material for a targeted attack

acceptanceCriteria.description: The rendered status page contains no host identifiers, no replica identifiers, no database identifiers, no queue names, no internal URLs, and no build hashes anywhere in its markup or its script tags; a grep of the fully-rendered document for a known internal identifier of each class returns zero matches.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the running process has known values for each identifier class (host name H, replica id R, database identifier D, queue name Q, internal URL U, build hash B)
acceptanceCriteria.when: the fully-rendered status page document is fetched and grepped for each of H, R, D, Q, U, and B
acceptanceCriteria.then: every grep returns zero matches, including inside script tags and inline JSON payloads

acceptanceCriteria.description: The rendered status page contains no raw metric values: no request counts, no latency numbers, no error rates, no queue depths appear as text or as data attributes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the running process is emitting internal metrics with known non-zero values
acceptanceCriteria.when: the rendered status page document is inspected for numeric content outside the incident notice startedAt timestamps
acceptanceCriteria.then: no metric value from the internal metric surface appears as text content or data attribute on any element

acceptanceCriteria.description: The readiness probe body may name declared dependencies (that is its purpose); the status page must not name them. The declared-component vocabulary and the declared-readiness-dependency vocabulary are distinct sets, and no declared readiness dependency name appears on the public status page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the process declares a readiness dependency set with distinct names from the declared status-page component set
acceptanceCriteria.when: the public status page is fetched and grepped for each declared readiness dependency name
acceptanceCriteria.then: every grep returns zero matches; a grep of the readiness probe body for the same names returns non-zero matches, demonstrating the surfaces are distinct
